evidence: The section occurs in the submitted Part 1 ontology report.

content_blocks.content:
1. Overview
The ontology models the structure of sandwiches that captures the whole (Sandwich), its parts
(BreadSlice, LayerOfFilling, Filling), and six variants
(SingleDeckerSandwich, DoubleDeckerSandwich, OpenSandwich,
ToastedSandwich, Panini, ClubSandwich).
I also created ﬁve object properties describe how these elements are related: hasBreadSlice that
links a sandwich to each slice of bread; hasLayer links a sandwich to each vertical layer of ﬁlling;
hasFillingIngredient links a layer to any ﬁlling substance (hasMeatFilling and
hasVegetableFilling)

evidence: The section occurs in the submitted Part 1 ontology report.

content_blocks.content:
2. Justiﬁcation
For classes, Sandwich is placed directly under owl:Thing; everything that is a sandwich inherits
from it.
Then, SingleDeckerSandwich, DoubleDeckerSandwich, OpenSandwich,
ToastedSandwich, Panini, ClubSandwich are declared subclasses of Sandwich because
each one is a sandwich with additional constraints.
BreadSlice, LayerOfFilling, and Filling remain siblings of Sandwich because they
are parts of a sandwich, not specialised sandwiches themselves.
For properties, hasBreadSlice and hasLayer are general relations from a sandwich to its
components, so they have no parent other than owl:topObjectProperty.
hasFillingIngredient is a relation from a layer to any ﬁlling. hasMeatFilling and
hasVegetableFilling are declared sub-properties of hasFillingIngredient.

evidence: The section occurs in the submitted Part 1 ontology report.

content_blocks.content:
3. Axiom
For SingleDeckerSandwich the ontology contains hasBreadSlice exactly 2
BreadSlice and hasLayer exactly 1 LayerOfFilling . This mean every
SingleDeckerSandwich must have exactly two bread slices and exactly one deck of ﬁlling.

For DoubleDeckerSandwich the ontology contains hasBreadSlice exactly 3
BreadSlice and hasLayer exactly 2 LayerOfFilling . This mean every
DoubleDeckerSandwich has exactly three slices and two decks of ﬁlling.

evidence: The section occurs in the submitted Part 1 ontology report.

content_blocks.content:
4. Advantages and disadvantages
The advantages of this ontology focuses on the structural and compositional aspects of a sandwich, like
how many slices of bread it has, how many ﬁlling layers, and the distinction between meat and
vegetable ingredients. This will help it to keep a clear and focused scope.
The disadvantage of this structure is that there is little further subdivision of the variants. All variants are
below Sandwich, it can be harder to capture more detailed groupings or shared behaviour among
subsets of sandwiches.
